title: JGB yield curve forecast — Main Forecast
date: Forecast vintage August 2026 · monthly, July 2026 – July 2029
standfirst: The JMA yield-curve model's forecast under our central case for Bank of Japan policy: two 25 basis point increases, in October 2026 and March 2027, to a terminal rate of 1.50 per cent. Spot JGB yields at 5 to 40 years, monthly to July 2029, with a one-standard-deviation uncertainty band.
stamp: Forecast vintage: August 2026, model origin July 2026. Estimates are revised periodically, and updated estimates are available for paid users upon request.
intro_html: The JMA yield curve model splits each JGB yield into interest-rate expectations and a term premium, letting Japan’s long-run interest rate move with its fundamentals. This page carries the forecast under our Main scenario. The model itself — what it is, what goes into it, and the historical decomposition it produces — is set out on the JGB yield curve model page. The charts below are interactive. Hover for exact values, zoom, and download the data behind each chart.
bottom_banner: The charts and data on this page are free to use and reproduce with attribution to Japan Macro Advisors. Only paid subscribers have access to this page. We will update our yield curve model estimates periodically, but in case the published estimate is more than 2 weeks old, paid subscribers can request an updated estimate and we should be able to reply within 2 business days.

items.head: Bank of Japan policy.
items.text: The policy rate is 1.00 per cent at the forecast origin. It rises by 25 basis points in October 2026 and by a further 25 basis points in March 2027, reaching a terminal rate of 1.50 per cent and staying there for the rest of the horizon.

items.head: The US term premium.
items.text: The forecast carries an assumed rise in the US 10-year term premium — the extra compensation demanded for holding long-dated Treasuries — following the change of Federal Reserve chair at the end of May 2026. It builds from 67 basis points at end-May 2026 to a peak of 122 basis points at end-November 2026, then unwinds part-way, with half the rise retained at 95 basis points by the end of the horizon. In our model, about a quarter of a US term-premium move passes through into superlong JGB yields.

items.head: The shaded band.
items.text: The band around each forecast path is a one-standard-deviation range built from the historical distribution of twelve-month moves in the US 10-year term premium. By 2029 it spans roughly plus or minus 17 basis points at 10 years and 20 basis points at 30 years. It is an uncertainty range around the US term-premium assumption alone, not a confidence interval around the whole forecast.

items.head: Origin and vintage.
items.text: The forecast runs monthly from July 2026 to July 2029. It is cut from a July 2026 month-end origin, which is a later starting point than the 19 July 2026 vintage published on the model page, so the starting yields on the two pages differ slightly.

sibling.label: Alternative Forecast: Faster and Further
sibling.text: The same model with the Bank of Japan moving sooner and going higher — three increases to a 1.75 per cent terminal rate.
